title: What Wren Gave Away
player_facing_question: Who supplied the Record with the company's names, plans, routes, and fears—and what does motive change once the act is proven?
plausible_initial_belief: The Record inferred everything from observation, or frightened Wren accidentally repeated one route detail while partially absorbed.
human_stake: Wren betrayed people who trusted him because he believed closure would erase what remained of him. Ash, Rook, and mkept deserve factual attribution; Wren deserves judgment after proof, not before it.
earned_belief: Wren deliberately transmitted names, operational plans, route changes, and private fears to preserve himself. The Record constrained him but did not originate every packet. Understanding his fear neither erases nor dictates judgment.
required_inference: Players attribute each leaked category by who knew it and when, distinguish deliberate transmission from passive observation, test Wren's claims against Rook's physical counter-proof, then choose remembrance without a hidden correct morality.
callback: Ash's joking shot list, mkept's offline windows, Rook's private marks, and Wren's changing distance all become attribution evidence. The apparently incidental phrase 'more distance' is re-read as fear of leaving observed space.

consequence.minecraft: Rook's counter-mark opens the Protocol Bridge route independent of Wren. The protected ballot commits condemn, understand, or free without changing the facts or bridge usability.
consequence.npc: Wren's final case line varies by remembrance treatment while the stable factual dialogue remains replayable.
consequence.copperline: A removed comment returns only its moderation chronology; later findings and remembrance attach without manufacturing a confession.
consequence.discord: The transmission finding is committed before the separate physical remembrance choice.

spaces.affordance: chronology columns accept theory drafts while source panels stay readable without receipt gating

spaces.affordance: seated NPC, visible topic papers, and always-open exit communicate conversation rather than confinement

evidence.title: Who heard it first
evidence.author: Ash and mkept
evidence.provenance: messages and camp notes distinguish spoken-only from written details
evidence.content: Three Watcher phrases repeat questions Ash, mkept, and Rook asked only with Wren present. None appears in a public note. Wren is the only common listener, but opportunity alone does not prove transmission.
evidence.clue_job: Establishes exclusive opportunity while explicitly withholding intent.

evidence.title: Camera and offline exclusions
evidence.author: Ash and server journal
evidence.medium: shot timestamps and local uptime receipt
evidence.provenance: Ash visible on fixed footage during packet 2; mkept server offline receipt covers packet 1
evidence.content: Ash could not send the locker schedule while filming the sealed camera run. mkept's admin client was offline when the login route packet appeared. These facts narrow authorship without relying on anyone's character claim.

evidence.title: Rook's private revision custody
evidence.author: Rook
evidence.provenance: revision shared only with Wren before packet; counter-mark never entered Record-facing plan
evidence.content: Rook changed the north brace and told Wren in person. The Spool packet contains the changed route but lacks the counter-mark Rook kept physical. That asymmetry identifies the channel and later tests Wren's directions.
evidence.accessibility: mark described by shape and text
evidence.clue_job: Proves the packet came through Wren's knowledge, not direct copying of Rook's complete plan.

evidence.title: Four packet progression
evidence.author: Wren channel; recipients recorded by Spool
evidence.provenance: stable packet ids and increasing specificity; no missing waveform required
evidence.content: Packet 1 names mkept and login window. Packet 2 gives Ash's cache schedule. Packet 3 gives Rook's changed bridge route. Packet 4 lists private fears by person. The progression is curated disclosure, not one accidental utterance.
evidence.clue_job: Establishes deliberate transmission of names, plans, routes, and fears.

evidence.title: Wren on distance
evidence.author: Wren
evidence.provenance: topic unlocked by established packet finding, not source clicks
evidence.content: When I went beyond its rooms I lost minutes first, then words. I thought closing it would make the gaps continuous. I told it where you would stand so it would keep a place for me. I knew those places belonged to you too.
evidence.accessibility: captioned text dialogue; no voice recognition or timing gate
evidence.clue_job: Explains motive while retaining agency and harm.

evidence.title: Wren's minimizing account
evidence.author: Wren
evidence.provenance: stable factual topics; replay cannot alter committed judgment
evidence.content: Wren first says the Record already knew. Confronted with Rook's absent counter-mark and Ash's sealed schedule, he corrects himself: It knew because I made knowing cheaper than letting me disappear.
evidence.accessibility: all topic choices keyboard/readable; stable transcript after conversation
evidence.clue_job: Secures admission without making confession the sole proof.

evidence.title: Rook's independent Bridge proof
evidence.author: Rook
evidence.medium: physical reverse-face marks and sealed component
evidence.provenance: counter-mark predates Wren confrontation; unique Protocol Bridge PDC/custody id
evidence.content: The three reverse-face marks align with Rook's retained carbon, not the route Wren describes. Opening them yields the Protocol Bridge and proves the route without trusting his admission. The component remains usable under every judgment.
evidence.accessibility: diagram alternative and assisted interaction; no block-perfect alignment
evidence.clue_job: Protects factual completion and future access from moral branch choice.

conclusions.prompt: What was transmitted, by whom, and why is it deliberate?
accepted_answers: Wren deliberately transmitted the company's names, plans, changed routes, and private fears in progressively specific packets; the Record did not passively infer the private revision.

conclusions.prompt: What motive does Wren admit, and what does it not erase?
accepted_answers: Wren feared that closing the Record would erase his partially retained self, but he chose to preserve himself by betraying the others; his fear explains the act without removing responsibility.

conclusions.prompt: Record the group's remembrance of Wren.

meaningful_wrong_theories.theory: The Record observed the plan directly and Wren only heard it repeat him.
meaningful_wrong_theories.response: The board acknowledges Record observation, then returns the absent physical counter-mark, sealed Ash schedule, and progressive packet order that require selective transmission.

meaningful_wrong_theories.theory: Wren acted under total compulsion and has no agency.
meaningful_wrong_theories.response: Constraint and memory gaps are accepted. His own correction and the curated packet sequence still establish choices about what and when to disclose.

meaningful_wrong_theories.theory: Wren's fear was selfish, so condemnation is the correct answer.
meaningful_wrong_theories.response: The factual finding is complete. The archive refuses to score remembrance; condemn, understand, and free remain intentional valid judgments.

hints.H0: Separate opportunity, transmission, admission, independent verification, and judgment.
hints.H1: For each leaked detail, ask who knew it first and whether the Record-facing copy contained it.
hints.H2: Rook's missing counter-mark is as important as the route detail the packet includes.
hints.H3: Wren is the only listener across the private phrases; packet progression proves deliberate disclosure; use Rook's physical marks for the Bridge; then choose remembrance without looking for a correct branch.

runtime.replay: stable factual transcript separated from immutable judgment receipt
runtime.restart: open dialogue topics and uncommitted ballots persist; committed judgment cannot duplicate or change
runtime.outage: local matrix and dialogue transcript remain authoritative; Discord mirrors contributors when available

novelty_comparison: P9 infers absent people through belongings and media. P10 is live attribution and adversarial conversation followed by moral judgment; the independent Bridge proof prevents confession from becoming a dialogue password.
cold_theory_paths: Record knew -> Wren channel -> deliberate betrayal
monster Wren -> frightened constrained person -> responsible frightened person
find culprit -> hear motive -> debate remembrance
